caption:
Two point eight million impressions last quarter. Zero of them you can trace to a client.

That is not a bad quarter. That is most quarters, almost everywhere, and it is the single most expensive thing in small-business marketing — not wasted spend, but unattributed spend. You cannot cut what you cannot see, so you end up cutting at random, usually the thing that was working.

Here is what we actually do about it.

There are five stages between someone seeing you and someone signing with you. Paid traffic buys the attention. Content earns the click before you have to pay for it. A funnel catches the lead before it cools. A site converts instead of explaining. Tracking tells you which half worked.

Most businesses buy one of those five and hope the other four happen on their own. Then the ads person blames the site, the site person blames the copy, the copy person blames the offer, and nobody can tell you what a client costs.

One system. One person accountable for the number at the end.

What the first thirty days look like, so there is no mystery month:

Week 1 — tracking goes in and we find the leak
Week 2 — offer and page rebuilt around one promise
Week 3 — traffic on, small, with a kill number agreed before we spend
Week 4 — the first report: booked calls, cost per client, what changes next

We do not report impressions. If a number is bad you hear it from us before you find it yourself, because the alternative is you discovering it in your bank account three months later.

The question that starts every project is the one on the last slide: where did your last ten clients come from? Almost nobody can answer it. Answering it is usually worth more than the next ad campaign.

Twenty minutes, free, whether you hire us or not — you leave with the list of what is leaking.
